items.title: Tanker struck by unknown projectile 11 nm west of Oman's Bukha; fire extinguished, crew safe
items.summary: UKMTO said Wednesday (Oct 21) an unknown projectile struck a tanker 11 nautical miles west of Bukha, Oman, overlooking the Strait of Hormuz. A fire erupted but was extinguished; the vessel is at anchor and all crew are reported safe. UKMTO disclosed no vessel name, flag, cargo or destination; no country or group has claimed responsibility. Al Arabiya English carried the report as breaking news.

items.title: Gulf oil exports topped prewar levels despite Hormuz attacks, per WSJ/Kpler
items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reports Middle East oil flows (through Hormuz plus alternate routes) averaged over 24 million barrels/day in the week through Oct 18, surpassing prewar levels of 23.3M b/d, per ship tracker Kpler — as an improvised US-protected shipping system keeps tankers moving. Flows through Hormuz itself (incl. Gulf of Oman offshore transfers) averaged ~14M b/d, about 82% of prewar; ~40% of non-Iranian Gulf crude bypassed the strait via Saudi/UAE pipelines in Sept (vs 17% prewar). Brent held ~$108/bbl Tuesday. Windward counts ~30 vessel attacks in October — about 20% of all war-to-date ship attacks. WSJ notes Iran's ability to deter transits has faded, weakening Tehran's leverage.
